e-ap-se.name: Eastern ducks · AP geese · Sept. East
e-ap-se.bounds: Duck zones: Eastern — Anne Arundel, Calvert, Caroline, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Harford, Kent, Queen Anne’s, St. Mary’s, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico and Worcester counties and the parts of Baltimore, Howard, Prince George’s and Montgomery counties east of the line; Western — Allegany, Carroll, Garrett, Frederick and Washington counties and the parts of those four counties west of it. The line: I-83 south from the Pennsylvania line to I-695 (Outer Loop), I-695 south to I-95, I-95 south to I-495 (Outer Loop), I-495 to the Virginia shore of the Potomac. Atlantic Population goose zone: Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Calvert, Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Harford, Howard, Kent, Queen Anne’s, Somerset, St. Mary’s, Talbot, Wicomico and Worcester counties; Carroll east of Route 31 to Route 97 and east of Route 97 to the Pennsylvania line; Prince George’s east of Routes 3 and 301; Charles east of Route 301. September resident goose (and teal) zones: DNR’s Eastern and Western early zones — Eastern takes the Eastern Shore and southern counties and the parts of Anne Arundel, Prince George’s and Charles east of the listed routes; Western takes Allegany, Baltimore, Carroll, Frederick, Garrett, Howard, Montgomery and Washington and the rest of those three.
e-ap-se.note: Eastern duck dates; Atlantic Population geese (2 a day); September geese Sept 1–15 and September teal Sept 17–26.

seasonsNote: No Sunday hunting for migratory game birds in Maryland. The guide still marks 2026–27 dates “contingent upon USFWS approval”; DNR says they are final.

seasons.label: Ducks
seasons.note: Black ducks only Nov 14–27 (Western Nov 21–27) and Dec 15 – Jan 30.

seasons.label: Sea ducks
seasons.note: No separate sea duck season; DNR keeps the Sea Duck Zone on its map (it matters for the late light goose segment).

seasons.label: Teal — September
seasons.note: September teal zone (DNR’s map; the app uses the Eastern early goose zone, which DNR draws almost identically).

seasons.label: Canada geese — early
seasons.note: Resident geese: Eastern early zone Sept 1–15, Western Sept 1–25.

seasons.label: Canada geese — regular
seasons.note: AP zone 2 a day. Late Southern: 5 a day Nov 21–23, then 2. Late Western: 5 a day. Late zones include cackling and white-fronted geese.

seasons.label: Canada geese — late
seasons.note: Late Southern Maryland resident zone, 5 a day.

seasons.label: Snow geese — late
seasons.note: Light Goose Eastern Zone only (the AP zone, Charles east of Route 301), and not in the Sea Duck Zone.

bags.detail: Six ducks a day, mergansers and sea ducks included, inside which the species limits below apply. Possession three times the daily limit.
Mergansers count in the 6-duck bag; no separate limit.
Inside the 6: no more than 3 scoters, 3 long-tailed ducks or 3 eiders (1 hen).
AP zone 2 (6). Late Southern 5 (15) Nov 21–23, then 2 (6). Late Western 5 (15).
Clapper and king rails; no more than 1 king a day (3 in possession).
6 ducks with the sub-limits, 1 brant, 2 AP or 5 resident geese, 15 coots, 25 light geese.

duckSublimits.note: only in the black duck season (Nov 14–27 Eastern / Nov 21–27 Western, and Dec 15 – Jan 30)
no more than 3 scoters, 3 long-tailed ducks or 3 eiders (1 hen)

rules.d: It is unlawful to hunt migratory game birds on Sunday in Maryland.

One-half hour before sunrise to sunset for ducks, coots, geese and brant. Doves Sept 1 – Oct 17: noon to sunset. The guide’s two pages differ on whether the late light goose segment runs to half an hour after sunset — check DNR.
Required for waterfowl and coots. No lead shot, and nothing larger than size T (0.20 inch).
An offshore (stationary) blind or blind site in public waters needs a $20 Stationary Blind and Blind Site licence, issued by lottery and online appointment.
No permanent blinds or tree stands, and no decoys left out overnight, on land DNR owns or controls, without DNR’s written permission.

Maryland keeps its Sea Duck Zone on the map but no longer has a separate sea duck season: sea ducks count in the 6-duck bag statewide. The late light goose segment (Feb 8 – Mar 10) is closed inside the Sea Duck Zone.
The guide marks 2026–27 dates “contingent upon approval from the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service”; DNR’s waterfowl page says they have been finalised in the Federal Register.
November 7, 2026 and February 6, 2027, statewide, with the bag limits above.
Leave the head or one fully feathered wing on until you get home, and tag birds left with anyone else (federal rules).

licences.d: $35 resident; $160 non-resident; $65 non-resident 3-day waterfowl and small game.

licences.t: Maryland Migratory Game Bird Stamp (with HIP)
licences.d: $15 — a printed validation that includes HIP certification.
$25 from refuges, post offices or online; $29 through MD Outdoors, a DNR service centre or a sport agent.

licences.t: Stationary Blind and Blind Site licence

closedNote: Maryland does not publish a statewide list of waters closed to waterfowl. Check the area you plan to hunt.
geometryNote: Geometry: Maryland DNR zone layers (late goose zones on US 301, MD 3, MD 97, MD 31 and county lines; the September Eastern/Western line including DNR’s line across the upper bay), OpenStreetMap (the Eastern/Western duck line on I-83, I-695, I-95 and I-495; numbered routes), Maryland iMAP (DNR lands, public water access), USGS NHD (water; streams from NHDPlus V2 small-scale because the high-resolution service was down on 2026-10-30), USFWS (refuge units; NWI marsh), NOAA CO-OPS (tides), Census TIGER (state outline, county subdivisions, shared borders). The September teal zone is drawn as DNR’s Eastern early goose zone, which DNR maps almost identically.
